_comment: Useful phrases (Redemittel) by speech act: agreeing, disagreeing, doubting, comforting … Each set is a flashcard deck (/vocabolario/espressioni/<id>) and a row under the phrases on /pronunciation. The key `de` holds the Italian phrase that is practised (the key name is history, see docs/content-plan.md §1.4); `en` is the English meaning, with a short usage note where it helps. Both address forms are taught: the phrase is written in the form most learners need first, and the note gives the other one (tu with friends and colleagues, Lei with officials, doctors and strangers). Every phrase has `variety` ("it-IT"); a `regional` note goes on a phrase only where a learner meets a real difference in daily life (none yet). Phrase order matters: the beginner path can refer to phrases as redemittel:<set>#<index>. Translations live in src/data/redemittel-i18n/<lang>.json, keyed by the Italian phrase: machine drafts until a native speaker has read them (reviewed: false). Audio: scripts/generate-satz-audio.mjs → public/audio/redemittel/<slug>.mp3 (none yet for the Italian phrases).

phrases.en: You're right. (To someone you call Lei: Ha ragione.)
I completely agree.
Exactly!
I agree with you. (With Lei: Sono d'accordo con Lei.)
I think so too.
That's exactly what I think.
That sounds like a good idea.
OK, agreed. Va bene is the everyday “OK” in Italy.
I see it differently.
I don't agree.
That's not quite right.

phrases.de: Mi dispiace, ma non sono d'accordo.
phrases.en: I'm sorry, but I disagree. A polite way to say no.
I don't think that's true. (After non credo che comes the subjunctive: sia.)
I don't think so.
Yes, but … You agree a little, then add your point.
No way! (informal)
I'm not so sure about that. (A woman says: sicura.)
Do you really think so? (To someone you call Lei: Lo pensa davvero?)
I don't know, I'm not sure. (A woman says: sicura.)
Is that really so? (After sei sicuro che comes the subjunctive: sia. To a woman: Sei sicura?)
I find that hard to believe.
Hmm, I have my doubts.
Are you sure? (To a woman: Sei sicura? To Lei: È sicuro?)
I doubt it.
I'm so sorry.
Cheer up! Keep going!
It'll be all right.
Don't worry. (To someone you call Lei: Non si preoccupi.)

phrases.de: Io ci sono, per qualsiasi cosa.
phrases.en: I'm here for whatever you need.
It's not that bad. Careful: with a real problem it can sound dismissive.
You can do it!
Is there anything I can do for you? (With Lei: Posso fare qualcosa per Lei?)
My view is that …
I think that … The easiest way to give your opinion. (Often followed by the subjunctive: Penso che sia giusto.)
In my opinion, …
It seems to me that … (Followed by the subjunctive: Mi sembra che sia vero.)
What matters to me is that … (Followed by the subjunctive.)
To be honest, … (A woman says: sincera.)
That's fine with me.
What do you think? (To someone you call Lei: Lei che ne pensa?)
Sorry? You didn't hear what someone said. (With tu: Scusa, come?)
Could you say that again, please? (With tu: Puoi ripetere?)

phrases.de: Può parlare più lentamente, per favore?
phrases.en: Could you speak more slowly, please? (With tu: Puoi parlare più lentamente?)
What does that mean?
Sorry, I didn't understand that. (With tu: Scusa, non ho capito.)
How do you spell that?
Do you mean that …? You check that you have understood. (With tu: Vuoi dire che …?)
Could you give me an example? (With tu: Mi puoi fare un esempio?)
Could you help me, please? A polite way to ask. (With tu: Mi puoi aiutare?)
Have you got a minute? (With tu: Hai un momento?)

phrases.de: Mi passi il sale, per favore?
phrases.en: Could you pass me the salt, please? (This form works with tu and with Lei.)
Could I ask you a favour? (With tu: Posso chiederti un favore?)
Sorry to bother you. Say this before you interrupt someone.
Could you show me? (With tu: Me lo puoi mostrare?)
I need some help.
Would that be possible?
Sorry! For a small mistake, or when you bump into someone. (To someone you call Lei: Scusi!)
I'm really sorry.
I didn't mean it like that.
Sorry I'm late. (With Lei: Scusi il ritardo.)
That was my fault.
No problem. An answer to an apology: it's OK.
It doesn't matter. An answer to an apology: forget it.
It could happen to anyone. An answer to an apology.
Thank you very much!
Thanks, that's very kind of you. (With Lei: è molto gentile.)

phrases.de: Grazie infinite per il tuo aiuto.
phrases.en: Thank you so much for your help. (With Lei: per il Suo aiuto.)
How thoughtful of you! For a small gift or a kind gesture.
You're welcome! An answer to thank you.
It was my pleasure. An answer to thank you.
Don't mention it. An answer to thank you.
I really appreciate it. (A woman says: grata. With Lei: Gliene sono molto grato.)
How about …? (Che ne dici se andiamo in metro? With Lei: Che ne direbbe se …?)
Shall we go out for a meal?
I suggest that we … (Followed by an infinitive: Propongo di prendere la metro.)

phrases.de: Ti va di andare al cinema?
phrases.en: Do you fancy going to the cinema? (Informal. With Lei: Le va di andare al cinema?)
Good idea, let's do that! A yes to a suggestion.

phrases.de: Mi dispiace, quel giorno non posso.
phrases.en: Sorry, I can't make it that day. A no to a suggestion.
Maybe another time.
Is Saturday good for you? (With Lei: Le va bene sabato?)
Congratulations! For an exam, a new job, a baby. (Complimenti! is also common.)
Happy birthday!
Good luck!

phrases.de: In bocca al lupo per l'esame!
phrases.en: Good luck with your exam! The usual answer is Crepi! (Don't say grazie.)
Get well soon! To someone who is ill.
Have a nice weekend! Said on Friday.
Merry Christmas!
I'm so happy for you!
Good morning! Used until lunchtime; in the afternoon people switch to Buonasera.
Nice to meet you. (With Lei: Piacere di conoscerLa. Often just: Piacere!)
How are you? Answer: Bene, grazie. E tu? (With Lei: Come sta?)
Long time no see! (informal)
See you tomorrow!
Goodbye! A polite goodbye; with friends: Ciao!
Take care! A friendly goodbye.
Have a good day!
In the picture I can see … The easiest way to start.

phrases.de: La foto mostra una famiglia a tavola.
phrases.en: The picture shows a family having a meal. You say what it is about.
In the foreground you can see …
In the background there's a park.
In the middle there's a table.

phrases.de: A sinistra c'è una giovane donna seduta.
phrases.en: On the left there's a young woman sitting down.

phrases.de: In alto a destra c'è una finestra.
phrases.en: In the top right-hand corner there's a window.

phrases.de: Probabilmente le persone sono in vacanza.
phrases.en: The people are probably on holiday. A guess about the situation.

phrases.de: Credo che sia una festa di compleanno.
phrases.en: I think it's a birthday party. A guess about the situation. (After credo che comes the subjunctive: sia.)
It looks as if everyone is happy. (After sembra che comes the subjunctive.)
The atmosphere is relaxed.

phrases.de: La foto mi ricorda la mia infanzia.
phrases.en: The picture reminds me of my childhood. You connect it with your own life.
The ball is in the box. (In + la = nella.)
The ball is on the box. (Su + la = sulla.)

phrases.de: La palla è sotto il tavolo.
phrases.en: The ball is under the table.

phrases.de: La lampada è appesa sopra il tavolo.
phrases.en: The lamp is hanging above the table. (Sopra means “above”; su means “on”.)

phrases.de: La palla è accanto alla scatola.
phrases.en: The ball is next to the box. (A + la = alla.)

phrases.de: La palla è davanti alla scatola.
phrases.en: The ball is in front of the box.

phrases.de: La palla è dietro la scatola.
phrases.en: The ball is behind the box.

phrases.de: La palla è tra le scatole.
phrases.en: The ball is between the boxes.

phrases.de: Il quadro è appeso al muro.
phrases.en: The picture is on the wall. (A + il = al.)
